Q1Physics
subjectPhysics
chapterRotational Motion high confidence
why this chapterThe answer depends on computing the moment of inertia of the disc minus the hole, using the disc formula and the parallel axis theorem, which is rotational motion.
subtopic 1Moment of Inertia of a Circular Shape
subtopic 2Parallel Axis and Perpendicular Axis Theorem
why this subtopicThe answer 13MR^2/32 comes from subtracting the removed small disc's moment of inertia (MR^2/2 form for a disc), shifted to the centre with the parallel axis theorem, from the full disc's MR^2/2.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
From a disc of radius R and mass M, a circular hole of diameter R, whose rim passes through the centre is cut. What is the moment of inertia of the remaining part of the disc about a perpendicular axis, passing through the centre?
  1. 15 MR2/32
  2. 13 MR2/32
  3. 11 MR2/32
  4. 9 MR2/32
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
  1. I = MR22 - 3σ2π(R2)2(R2)2
  2. Where σ = Mπ R2
  3. I = MR22 - 332MR2
  4. I = 1332MR2

→ the working concludes: option 2

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 2 · high
  1. The hole has radius r = R/2, so its mass is m = M(R/2)2R2 = M4.
  2. MI of the hole about its own centre: Ic = 12 m r2 = 12·M4·R24 = MR232.
  3. The hole's centre is at distance R/2 from the disc centre, so by the parallel axis theorem IO = MR232 + M4(R2)2 = 3MR232.
  4. Full disc: Idisc = 12MR2 = 16MR232.
  5. Remaining: I = 16MR232 - 3MR232 = 13MR232, which is option 2.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
22 highagree
difficultyhard · 4 steps
stepsfind the mass of the removed disc from the area ratio (radius R/2, so one quarter of the area and mass) → write the moment of inertia of the removed disc about its own centre using MR2/2 with mass M/4 and radius R/2 → shift that moment of inertia to the axis through the big disc's centre with the parallel-axis theorem (offset R/2) → subtract the removed part's moment of inertia from MR2/2 of the full disc
whyThe work is a mass-from-area scaling, a standard disc moment of inertia, a parallel-axis shift and a subtraction, chained so each feeds the next.
the catchOne distractor is exactly the result of skipping the parallel-axis shift and subtracting the hole's moment of inertia about its own centre.

Q2Physics
subjectPhysics
chapterMagnetic Effect of Electric Current high confidence
why this chapterThe answer turns on the force between parallel current-carrying conductors (mu0 I i L / 2 pi d) acting on the near and far sides AB and CD of the loop, which is the magnetic effect of electric current.
subtopic 1Force Between Two Parallel Current-Carrying Conductors
why this subtopicThe net force comes from the force per unit length between the wire XY and the loop's parallel sides AB and CD (attraction at L/2 minus repulsion at 3L/2), which is the force between two parallel current-carrying conductors.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A square loop ABCD carrying a current i, is placed near and coplanar with a long straight conductor XY carrying a current I, the net force on the loop will be:
  1. 2μ0 Ii3π
  2. μ0 Ii2π
  3. 2μ0 IiL3π
  4. μ0 IiL2π
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (1)
  1. F1 = μ0 IiL2π L2 = μ0 Iiπ
  2. 2 = μ0 IiL2π 3L2 = μ0 Ii3π
  3. ∴ Fnet = F1 - F2
  4. Fnet = 23μ0 Iiπ

→ the working concludes: option 1

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 1 · high
  1. Forces on the perpendicular sides BC and DA are equal and opposite, so they cancel.
  2. Side AB is at distance L/2: FAB = μ0 I i L2π (L/2) = μ0 I iπ.
  3. Side CD is at distance 3L/2: FCD = μ0 I i L2π (3L/2) = μ0 I i3π.
  4. AB and CD carry opposite currents, so their forces are opposite: Fnet = μ0 I iπ - μ0 I i3π = 2μ0 I i3π, which is option 1.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
11 highagree
difficultymedium · 3 steps
stepsRecognise that the forces on the two sides perpendicular to the wire (BC and DA) are equal and opposite and cancel → Apply F = μ0 I i L / (2 π r) to the near side AB at r = L/2 and to the far side CD at r = 3L/2 → Note AB (parallel current) is attracted and CD (antiparallel) is repelled, and subtract the two magnitudes to get the net force
whyThe work is the standard force-between-parallel-currents formula applied to two sides at different distances, plus the symmetry argument that removes the perpendicular sides and a subtraction of the two results.
the catchTwo options carry an extra factor L, the result of forgetting that the side length L cancels against the distance L/2 and 3L/2; a dimension check removes them.

Q4Physics
subjectPhysics
chapterWaves high confidence
why this chapterThe answer turns on the Doppler effect: sound reaching the cliff from a source moving towards it, then reflected back to the observer, which is taught in Waves.
subtopic 1Doppler Effect
why this subtopicThe answer comes from the Doppler shift for a source moving towards the cliff, which acts as a stationary reflector, giving f' = 800 x 330/(330-15) = 838 Hz.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A siren emitting a sound of frequency 800 Hz moves away from an observer towards a cliff at a speed of 15 ms-1. Then, the frequency of sound that the observer hears in the echo reflected from the cliff is : (Take velocity of sound in air = 330 ms-1)
  1. 765 Hz
  2. 800 Hz
  3. 838 Hz
  4. 885 Hz
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (3)
  1. f0 = 800 Hz
  2. Vsource = 15 m/s
  3. fa = 330(330 - 15)800 = 330315 × 800
  4. fa = 838 Hz

→ the working concludes: option 3

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 3 · high
  1. The siren (source) moves towards the stationary cliff at vs = 15 m s-1, so the cliff receives f' = fvv - vs.
  2. f' = 800 × 330330 - 15 = 800 × 330315.
  3. f' = 838.1 Hz ≈ 838 Hz.
  4. The cliff is stationary and reflects f'; the observer is also stationary, so the echo is heard at 838 Hz, which is option 3.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
33 highagree
difficultymedium · 3 steps
stepsRecognise that the echo frequency is the frequency received at the cliff, with the siren moving towards the stationary cliff → Apply the Doppler formula for a source approaching a stationary observer: f' = f v / (v - v_s) → Note that the cliff re-emits f' as a stationary source to a stationary observer, so the observer hears f' unchanged, and evaluate 800 x 330 / 315
whyThe work is choosing the cliff as the effective receiver, applying the moving-source Doppler formula with the approaching sign, and seeing that the reflection adds no further shift.
the catchThe 765 Hz option is exactly the frequency of the direct sound from the receding siren, so a candidate who uses the 'moving away' sign gets a listed answer.

Q5Physics
subjectPhysics
chapterCapacitance high confidence
why this chapterThe answer turns on the energy lost when charge redistributes between a charged 2 uF capacitor and an uncharged 8 uF capacitor, which is taught under capacitance (energy stored in a capacitor, redistribution of charges).
subtopic 1Redistribution of Charges
why this subtopicThe answer depends on the energy lost when a charged 2 uF capacitor shares its charge with an uncharged 8 uF capacitor (loss fraction C2/(C1+C2) = 80%), which is taught under redistribution of charges.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A capacitor of 2 μF is charged as shown in the diagram. When the switch S is turned to position 2, the percentage of its stored energy dissipated is:
  1. 0%
  2. 20%
  3. 75%
  4. 80%
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (4)
  1. Q = 2V
  2. Ui = 12 × (2V)22 = V2
  3. ∴ Vy = 1264V225 × 8
  4. 2V - q2 = q8 + 124V225 × 2
  5. ∴ 8V - 4q = q
  6. Uf = 5V225 = V25
  7. ∴ q = 8V5
  8. Energy dissipated = 4V25
  9. ∴ % energy
  10. Dissipated = 4V25V2 × 100
  11. = 80%

→ the working concludes: option 4

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
  1. In position 1 the 2 μF capacitor charges to V: Ui = 12(2)V2 = V2 (in μJ units), Q = 2V.
  2. In position 2 it connects in parallel with the uncharged 8 μF capacitor; charge is conserved, so V' = QC1 + C2 = 2V10 = V5.
  3. Uf = 12(10)(V5)2 = V25.
  4. Energy dissipated = Ui - Uf = 45V2, i.e. Ui - UfUi = C2C1 + C2 = 810 = 80%, which is option 4.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
44 highagree
difficultymedium · 3 steps
stepsWrite the initial stored energy of the 2 uF capacitor charged to V: U_i = 12(2 uF)V2 → Use charge conservation when S connects it to the uncharged 8 uF capacitor to get the common voltage V' = 2V/(2+8) = V/5, and the final energy U_f = 12(10 uF)(V/5)2 → Form the dissipated fraction (U_i - U_f)/U_i and convert to a percentage (equivalently C2/(C1+C2))
whyThe work is a charge-sharing calculation: conserve charge to find the common potential, compute energy before and after, and take the fractional loss.
the catchOne distractor equals the fraction of energy retained rather than dissipated, so a candidate who computes U_f/U_i and stops picks it.

Q7Physics
subjectPhysics
chapterGravitation high confidence
why this chapterThe answer uses V = -GM/(R+h) and g = GM/(R+h)^2, so |V|/g = R+h = 9000 km gives h = 2600 km, which is gravitational potential and the variation of g with height.
subtopic 1Variation in g Due to Height and Rotation
subtopic 2Calculation of Gravitational Potential
why this subtopicThe answer combines V = -GM/(R+h) and g = GM/(R+h)^2 at height h, so R+h = |V|/g = 9000 km and h = 2600 km.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
At what height from the surface of earth the gravitation potential and the value of g are -5.4 × 107 J kg-2 and 6.0 ms-2 respectively? Take the radius of earth as 6400 km:
  1. 2600 km
  2. 1600 km
  3. 1400 km
  4. 2000 km
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (1)
  1. V = GMR + h = -5.4 × 107
  2. g = GM(R + h)2 = 6
  3. ∴ 5.46 × 107 = R + h
  4. ∴ a × 106 = 6.4 × 106 + h
  5. ∴ h = 2600 km

→ the working concludes: option 1

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 1 · high
  1. At distance r = R + h from the centre, V = -GMr and g = GMr2.
  2. Dividing, |V|g = GM/rGM/r2 = r.
  3. r = 5.4 × 1076.0 = 9.0 × 106 m = 9000 km.
  4. h = r - R = 9000 km - 6400 km = 2600 km, which is option 1.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
11 highagree
difficultymedium · 3 steps
stepsWrite the potential at distance r from the centre as V = -GM/r and the field there as g = GM/r2 → Divide |V| by g to eliminate GM, giving r = |V|/g → Substitute the given values to get r in km and subtract the earth's radius 6400 km to get the height
whyThe work is spotting that the ratio of potential to field strength gives the distance from the centre directly, then one division and one subtraction of the radius.

Q9Physics
subjectPhysics
chapterElectrostatics high confidence
why this chapterThe answer comes from balancing the Coulomb repulsion between the spheres against tension and gravity (kq^2/x^2 proportional to x for small angles, so q proportional to x^(3/2)), so it rests on Coulomb's law.
subtopic 1Coulomb's Law
why this subtopicThe answer comes from balancing the Coulomb repulsion kq^2/x^2 against the gravity component (mg x/2l), giving q proportional to x^(3/2), and a constant leak rate then gives v proportional to x^(-1/2).
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
Two identical charged spheres suspended from a common point by two massless strings of lengths l, are initially at a distance d(d << l) apart because of their mutual repulsion. The charges begin to leak from both the spheres at a constant rate. As a result, the spheres approach each other with a velocity υ. Then υ varies as a function of the distance x between the spheres, as
  1. υ ∝ x12
  2. υ ∝ x
  3. υ ∝ x-12
  4. υ ∝ x-1
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (3)
  1. θ = x2l
  2. fecosθ = mghλθ
  3. fe = mg.(x2)
  4. kq2x2 = mgx2e
  5. kq2 = mg2lx3
  6. q ∝ x32
  7. dqdt ∝ 32 x12.dxdt
  8. ⇒ x12.v = constant
  9. v ∝ x-12

→ the working concludes: option 3

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 3 · high
  1. For each sphere, balancing forces gives tanθ = Fmg with F = kq2x2.
  2. Since x ≪ l, tanθ ≈ sinθ = x/2l = x2l.
  3. x2l = kq2x2 mg ⇒ q2 = mg2lkx3 ⇒ q ∝ x3/2.
  4. Differentiate: dqdt ∝ 32x1/2dxdt.
  5. dqdt is constant, so υ = dxdt ∝ x-1/2, which is option 3.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
33 highagree
difficultyhard · 5 steps
stepsWrite force balance on one sphere: T cos(θ) = mg and T sin(θ) = kq2/x2, giving tan(θ) = kq2/(mg x2) → Apply the small-angle geometry tan(θ) ~ sin(θ) = (x/2)/l, using d << l → Combine to get q2 proportional to x3, i.e. q proportional to x^32 → Differentiate with respect to time: dq/dt proportional to x^12 dx/dt → Use the constant leak rate (dq/dt constant) to obtain v = dx/dt proportional to x^(-1/2)
whyThe candidate must set up the equilibrium of a charged pendulum, apply the small-angle approximation to relate charge to separation, and then differentiate that relation in time under a constant leak rate to extract the velocity's dependence on x.
the catchThe non-obvious move is treating the motion as a sequence of quasi-static equilibria and time-differentiating the q-x relation; the options x^(1/2) and x^(-1/2) differ only in sign of exponent, so a slip in rearranging the derivative lands on a distractor.

Q10Physics
subjectPhysics
chapterWaves high confidence
why this chapterThe answer turns on the speed of a transverse wave on a string, v = sqrt(T/mu), with tension rising from m2*g at the bottom to (m1+m2)*g at the top at fixed frequency, so wavelength scales as sqrt(T).
subtopic 1Speed of Different Waves
why this subtopicThe answer depends on the speed of a transverse wave on a string, v = sqrt(T/mu), with tension m2*g at the bottom and (m1+m2)*g at the top, so wavelength scales with sqrt(T) at fixed frequency.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A uniform rope of length L and mass m1, hangs vertically from a rigid support. A block of mass m2 is attached to the free end of the rope. A transverse pulse of wavelength λ1 is produced at the lower end of the rope. The wavelength of the pulse when it reaches the top of the rope is λ2. The ratio λ2/λ1 is:
  1. m1m2
  2. m1+m2m2
  3. m1m2
  4. m1+m2m1
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
  1. At bottom
  2. v1 = M2 g LM1
  3. ∴ λ1 = M2M1 g L 1f
  4. At top.
  5. ∴ λ2λ1 = M1 + M2M2
  6. v1 = (M1 + M2) g LM1
  7. ∴ λ2 = (M1 + M2) g LM1 1f

→ the working concludes: option 2

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 2 · high
  1. The frequency of the pulse is set by the source and does not change along the rope, so λ = vf ∝ v.
  2. Wave speed on the rope is v = Tμ with μ = m1L uniform, so λ ∝ T.
  3. At the lower end the rope supports only the block: T1 = m2 g.
  4. At the top the rope supports the block and the whole rope: T2 = (m1 + m2) g.
  5. λ2λ1 = T2T1 = m1 + m2m2, which is option 2.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict

difficultymedium · 3 steps
stepsFind the tension at each end of the rope: m2*g at the lower end (only the block hangs below) and (m1+m2)*g at the top (block plus the whole rope). → Relate wave speed to tension, v = T/μ, with the same linear mass density μ along the uniform rope. → Note that frequency stays fixed as the pulse travels, so wavelength scales with speed, and take the ratio of the square s of the two tensions.

READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A refrigerator works between 4°C and 30°C. It is required to remove 600 calories of heat every second in order to keep the temperature of the refrigerated space constant. The power required is: (Take 1 cal = 4.2 Joules)

  4. 2365 W

  1. 600 + w600 = 303277
  2. 1 + w600 = 1 + 26277
  3. w = 600 × 26277 × 4.2
  4. w = 236.5

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 3 · high
  1. TL = 4 + 273 = 277 K, TH = 30 + 273 = 303 K.
  2. Heat removed per second QL = 600 × 4.2 = 2520 J/s.
  3. For an ideal refrigerator β = QLW = TLTH - TL = 27726 ≈ 10.654.
  4. P = QLβ = 2520 × 26277 ≈ 236.5 W, which is option 3.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict

difficultymedium · 3 steps

    2. The H – O – H bond angle in H2O is larger than the H – C – H bond angle in CH4.
    3. The H – O – H bond angle in H2O is smaller than the H – N – H bond angle in NH3.
    4. The H – C – H bond angle in CH4 is larger than the H – N – H bond angle in NH3.
    The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
    1. Bond Angle | Molecule
    2. 104.5° | H2O
    3. 107° | NH3
    4. 109°28' | CH4
    5. All the molecules are sp3 hybridized and Bond angle of H2O is smaller than NH3.

    → the working concludes: option 2

    printed solution, as in the booklet

    3. NH3 has one lone pair: ∠ HNH ≈ 107°.
    4. H2O has two lone pairs: ∠ HOH ≈ 104.5°.
    5. Option 1: all angles > 90°, true. Option 3: 104.5° < 107°, true. Option 4: 109.5° > 107°, true.
    6. Option 2 claims 104.5° > 109.5°, which is false, so the answer is option 2.
